title: [News] NVIDIA’s NVHBM Reshapes Base Die Strategies: How Micron, Samsung Are Bringing TSMC Into the Fold
key_facts: Nvidia's NVHBM, announced in August, moves the memory controller into the HBM base die.
The Elec: Micron said NVHBM and JEDEC-standard HBM4E will use base dies from an external foundry; TSMC is expected to take the role.
ZDNet: Samsung is pursuing a dual track, pairing its memory dies with base dies from Samsung Foundry or TSMC depending on the customer.
Nvidia claims up to 30% more bandwidth, 15% lower HBM power and up to 25% more area freed on the compute die versus standard HBM4E.
Amazon's Annapurna Labs is set to adopt the technology for its Trainium 4 accelerator (ZDNet).
SK hynix already uses TSMC's 12nm process for its HBM4 base die; 3nm is prioritised for HBM4E and custom HBM (EDAILY).
quote_evidence: According to The Elec, Micron said both its NVHBM, co-designed with NVIDIA, and JEDEC-standard HBM4E will use base dies manufactured by an external foundry.
According to NVIDIA, NVHBM delivers up to 30% greater memory bandwidth and 15% lower HBM power consumption than standard HBM4E, while freeing up to 25% more area on the XPU compute die.
Under the new model, Samsung’s HBM core dies could be paired with base dies manufactured by either Samsung Foundry or foundry rival TSMC, depending on customer requirements, the report notes.
why_it_matters_hint: Memory makers shift base-die production to TSMC for custom HBM.
notes: TrendForce News curates other outlets' reports (The Elec, ZDNet, Newsis, EDAILY); chain of first reporters is named in the summary. Performance figures are attributed to NVIDIA.
